title: Lesson 72: Building the Platform: Control Plane, Data Plane, Gateway, and Policy Layer
description: How to construct the four pieces of an agent platform: the gateway that enforces policy in the traffic path, the policy decision point that makes allow or deny decisions, the control plane that governs identity and lifecycle, and the data plane that carries the agent's work.

questions.question: Why is the gateway the right place to enforce policy in an agent platform?
options: Because every request crosses it, so it can stop an action early.
Because it is the only component able to run the language model.
Because it stores all of the agent's long-term memory between its sessions.
Because it replaces the policy engine entirely, so no decision layer is needed.
questions.explanation: Policy written only in a design document stops nothing; it takes effect where traffic actually flows. Every agent request passes through the gateway, so it can authenticate the caller and halt an action before it reaches a model or tool.

questions.question: How are enforcement and decision-making divided between the gateway and the policy engine?
options: The gateway makes every allow or deny decision itself from hardcoded rules.
The policy engine sits in the request path and enforces what the gateway decides.
The gateway enforces; the policy engine evaluates and returns the decision.
Both are optional, since policy can live inside each agent's prompt.
questions.explanation: Separating the enforcement point from the decision point keeps the enforcement code simple and stable while the policy changes on its own. The gateway stays in the traffic path as the enforcer, and the policy engine returns the allow or deny decision.

questions.question: What does a default-deny policy rule accomplish in a policy layer built to govern agent actions?
options: It allows any action unless a policy explicitly forbids it.
It forbids any action unless a policy explicitly allows it.
It logs every action but blocks none of them at runtime.
It defers every decision to the agent's own prompt instructions.
questions.explanation: Default deny makes the safe path the default: an action is refused unless a policy explicitly permits it, and a forbid-wins rule means one denial stands even if another policy allows. That is the right bias when the actor is an agent you cannot fully predict.
